text:
Recent evidence supports separating sampled ranking quality from full-catalog behavior. RecSys 2025’s [On the Reliability of Sampling Strategies](https://doi.org/10.1145/3705328.3748086) finds that candidate sampling affects model separability, agreement with full evaluation, and robustness to exposure bias; sampled evaluation does not automatically recover underlying preference rankings. [Improved Estimation of Ranks (2024)](https://research.google/pubs/improved-estimation-of-ranks-for-learning-item-recommenders-with-negative-sampling/) likewise identifies bias from negative sampling. Healthy training margins therefore cannot establish strong appended-MASK ranking.

The [Does It Look Sequential? author repository (RecSys 2024)](https://github.com/Antondfger/Does-It-Look-Sequential/) reports inference-time shuffling experiments using HR@10, NDCG@10, recommendation-set Jaccard, and bootstrap significance checks. Sensitivity varies substantially across datasets. A suitable adaptation: freeze each BERT4Rec model; predict training-history prefix targets through appended MASK; compare recent-history deletion against repeated random deletion matched on removal count, plus reversal and shuffling. Preserve left padding and MASK placement, and hold targets and candidate sets constant across paired conditions. These proposed controls distinguish recency dependence, order dependence, and generic information loss; performance drops alone do not establish causal importance.

For candidate difficulty, compare fixed uniform negatives, popularity-stratified negatives, and full unseen-catalog ranking on identical prefixes; report target-popularity and history-length strata. Bootstrap users, retaining all prefixes and paired perturbations within each resampled user, to estimate 95% intervals for metric differences. Add identity-transform controls expecting zero change, synthetic score-order controls with known ranks, and deliberate readout/MASK corruptions to check probe sensitivity. These are proposed diagnostic safeguards, not established findings from the cited papers. Keep results separate from unchanged host validation HR@10; use only training histories and the existing single checkpoint per category.
